\section{Canonical equations and invariants}
\label{sec:equations}

\subsection{Admission and valid support}

Let \(\mathsf A_j\) be the conjunction of the scientific admission predicates:
the sample is upstream-eligible \code{xs}; its acquisition key and sample
column binding are resolved; its selected APT row and unique admitted
association are resolved; units and factor directions are declared; the
sample, baseline state, factor, opacity, airmass, time support, operator, and
response basis are valid for the requested operation; and the effective mode
is enabled. The mathematical domain is
\begin{equation}
  \valid=\{j:\mathsf A_j=\mathrm{true}\}.
  \label{eq:valid-support}
\end{equation}
Restriction to \(\valid\) is not multiplication by a Boolean mask. Invalid
occurrences do not become scientific zeros and do not contribute hits or
coverage.

The explicitly declared affine input is
\begin{equation}
  z_j=x^{xs}_j-b_j,\qquad j\in\valid.
  \label{eq:affine-input}
\end{equation}
If the upstream convention has no subtraction, its record says that the
baseline operation is not applicable and Equation~\eqref{eq:affine-input}
reduces explicitly to \(z_j=x^{xs}_j\). Missing baseline meaning is not that
state.

\subsection{Retained structural atmosphere operator}
\label{sec:atmos-equations}

The line-of-sight coordinate at the top-of-atmosphere pivot is
\begin{equation}
  \ell_{ot}=\tau_{225,o}(t)\,[X_{ot}-X_{\rm ref}]
  =\tau_{225,o}(t)X_{ot},\qquad X_{\rm ref}=0.
  \label{eq:los-coordinate}
\end{equation}
This is a coordinate for the retained operator, not a claim that a TolTEC
band opacity equals \(\tau_{225}\), nor permission to replace the retained
operator by an unapproved monochromatic exponential.

For each array, a complete content-bound record for \(\mathcal O_a\) must
declare strictly ordered nodes
\begin{equation}
  0=\ell_{a,0}<\ell_{a,1}<\cdots<\ell_{a,K_a},
  \qquad H_{a,0}=1,
  \label{eq:operator-nodes}
\end{equation}
their dimensionless ordinates \(H_{a,k}\), and one orientation
\(\sigma_a\in\{\mathrm{transmission},\mathrm{correction}\}\). On a closed
node interval,
\begin{align}
 u&=\frac{\ell-\ell_{a,k}}{\ell_{a,k+1}-\ell_{a,k}},
 \label{eq:operator-fraction}\\
 H_a(\ell)&=(1-u)H_{a,k}+uH_{a,k+1},
 \quad \ell\in[\ell_{a,k},\ell_{a,k+1}].
 \label{eq:piecewise-operator}
\end{align}
The canonical transmission and correction are then
\begin{equation}
 (T_a,C_a)=
 \begin{cases}
   (H_a,H_a^{-1}),&\sigma_a=\mathrm{transmission},\\
   (H_a^{-1},H_a),&\sigma_a=\mathrm{correction}.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:operator-orientation}
\end{equation}
Interpolation is applied to the authoritative ordinate before taking a
reciprocal. Interpolating the reciprocal instead is, in general, a different
operator and is not conformant.

The structural invariants are
\begin{equation}
 T_a(0)=C_a(0)=1,\qquad
 0<T_a(\ell)<1,\quad 1<C_a(\ell)<\infty
 \quad\text{for }0<\ell\leq\ell_{a,K_a},
 \label{eq:atmos-invariants}
\end{equation}
with \(T_a\) strictly decreasing and \(C_a\) strictly increasing on declared
support. Thus there is no positive-opacity unity plateau. Exact node values
are reproduced and the operator is continuous at every seam. Its derivative
may change discontinuously at a seam.

The authorized structural domain for a sample is the intersection
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal D_{otd}=\left\{
 0\leq\tau_{225,o}(t)\leq0.15,\quad
 X_{ot}\in\mathcal D_X,\quad
 0\leq\ell_{ot}\leq\ell_{a(d),K_{a(d)}},\quad
 t\in\mathcal D_\tau
 \right\},
 \label{eq:atmos-domain}
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal D_X\) is the declared upstream airmass-model domain and
\(\mathcal D_\tau\) is the opacity source's declared time support. A
time-resolved opacity at a sample is admissible only when measured at that
time or obtained by a source-authorized interpolation between bracketing
states whose declared validity covers the sample. No extrapolation from an
unbracketed endpoint is allowed. Equation~\eqref{eq:atmos-domain} is exact as a
support intersection, but cannot be numerically instantiated until the
operator record in \Assump{011} is supplied.

\subsection{Once-only signal factorization}
\label{sec:factor-equations}

The selected APT is the value boundary for absolute calibration. If TolProj
has materialized a pointing-derived correction, its causal ancestry may be
written
\begin{equation}
  F^{\rm sel}_{od}=P_{od}F^{\rm parent}_{od}
  \quad\text{(lineage identity only)}.
  \label{eq:embodied-pointing}
\end{equation}
The right-hand factors are not separately applied to the target signal.
Admissible correction dispositions are \code{not_applicable} and
\code{embodied_once}, with the parent and event identities present for the
latter. \code{required_but_unresolved} is not an admissible calibrated state.

Because v0.1 has only the target unit \(\mjybeam\), its unit-transfer factor is
the explicit identity \(Q_{\mjybeam}=1\). The exact realized multiplier and
signal are
\begin{align}
 M_j &= F^{\rm sel}_{od}\,C_{a(d)}(\ell_{ot})\,Q_{\mjybeam},
 \label{eq:multiplier}\\
 y_j &= M_j z_j,\qquad j\in\valid.
 \label{eq:signal}
\end{align}
No independent \code{responsivity}, \code{sens}, parent \code{flxscale},
pointing-derived correction, or opaque \code{fcf} appears in
Equation~\eqref{eq:multiplier}. Any such quantity used upstream may be named in
lineage or a nuisance model, but does not become another signal factor.

Numeric multiplication in Equation~\eqref{eq:multiplier} is commutative.
Causal provenance is not: the selected APT must exist before its row factor is
bound, and target atmosphere state is applied at the target sample. For each
factor role \(\rho\in\{\mathrm{absolute\ flxscale},
\mathrm{target\ atmosphere},\mathrm{unit\ identity}\}\), define the realized
application count \(n_{j\rho}\). The once-only invariant is
\begin{equation}
  n_{j\rho}=1\quad\text{for every required role and }j\in\valid,
  \label{eq:once-only}
\end{equation}
and zero for roles not in the canonical multiplier. The factor-instance
identities, not merely their numeric values, establish this count.

For a nonzero intended factor \(f\), challenge results relative to the correct
output obey
\begin{equation}
 \frac{y_{\rm omitted}}{y_{\rm correct}}=f^{-1},\qquad
 \frac{y_{\rm duplicated}}{y_{\rm correct}}=f,\qquad
 \frac{y_{\rm inverted}}{y_{\rm correct}}=f^{-2},
 \label{eq:factor-challenges}
\end{equation}
when all other quantities are fixed and the inverse replaces the intended
factor. A unity factor leaves values unchanged but must still retain its role
and instance identity when the role is required.

\subsection{Conditional measurement uncertainty}
\label{sec:conditional-uncertainty}

Stack the valid samples and let \(A=\diag(M_j)\). Conditioned on fixed state
\(\theta\),
\begin{align}
 \E[\boldsymbol y\mid\theta]
   &=A\{\E[\boldsymbol x^{xs}\mid\theta]-\boldsymbol b\},
 \label{eq:conditional-mean}\\
 C_{y\mid\theta}&=A C_{x\mid\theta}A^{\mathsf T}.
 \label{eq:conditional-covariance}
\end{align}
This transformation preserves every supplied sample, detector, and
observation correlation. For a diagonal conditional representation,
\begin{equation}
 v^{(y)}_j=M_j^2v^{(x)}_j,\qquad
 w^{(y)}_j=\frac{w^{(x)}_j}{M_j^2}.
 \label{eq:variance-weight}
\end{equation}
The valid support is identical to the signal support. If the corresponding
input uncertainty is absent, the output state is unavailable rather than a
zero variance or infinite weight.

Every synthetic injection, conditional noise realization, or genuine
raw-domain Jacobian companion \(k_{jr}=\partial x_j/\partial\alpha_r\) that is
declared to share the signal response obeys
\begin{equation}
 k^{(y)}_{jr}=M_j k^{(x)}_{jr}.
 \label{eq:companion-transfer}
\end{equation}
This equation does not authorize relabeling a physically distinct measured
stream as a response companion.

\subsection{Calibration and response nuisance covariance}
\label{sec:nuisance-equations}

For a fixed factor sign, let
\begin{equation}
 H_{jr}=\frac{\partial\ln|M_j|}{\partial\theta_r}.
 \label{eq:nuisance-jacobian}
\end{equation}
Within one atmosphere interpolation interval define
\begin{equation}
 \gamma_a(\ell)=\frac{d\ln C_a}{d\ell}
 =\begin{cases}
   -H'_a(\ell)/H_a(\ell),&\sigma_a=\mathrm{transmission},\\
   \phantom{-}H'_a(\ell)/H_a(\ell),&\sigma_a=\mathrm{correction}.
  \end{cases}
 \label{eq:atmos-log-slope}
\end{equation}
Hence, away from seams,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\partial\ln C_a}{\partial\tau_{225}}=\gamma_a X,
 \qquad
 \frac{\partial\ln C_a}{\partial X}=\gamma_a\tau_{225}.
 \label{eq:atmos-derivatives}
\end{equation}
For mean calibrated signal \(\boldsymbol\mu\), the first-order nuisance term is
\begin{equation}
 C_{\rm nuis}\simeq
 \diag(\boldsymbol\mu)H C_\theta H^{\mathsf T}
 \diag(\boldsymbol\mu).
 \label{eq:nuisance-covariance}
\end{equation}
It is generally dense. A common fractional absolute-scale uncertainty \(s\)
gives
\begin{equation}
 C_{\rm common}=s^2\boldsymbol\mu\boldsymbol\mu^{\mathsf T},
 \label{eq:common-rank-one}
\end{equation}
a rank-one contribution that does not decrease merely because more affected
samples are averaged.

If fitted calibration state or baseline depends on the same data, a first-
order total covariance also contains cross terms:
\begin{align}
 C_y\simeq{}& A C_x A^{\mathsf T}
 +J_\theta C_\theta J_\theta^{\mathsf T}
 +J_b C_bJ_b^{\mathsf T}
 +A C_{x\theta}J_\theta^{\mathsf T}
 +J_\theta C_{\theta x}A^{\mathsf T}
 +\text{other declared cross terms},
 \label{eq:full-covariance}
\end{align}
where \(J_b=-A\). Independence can remove a cross term only when justified.
Linearization is unavailable at an operator seam, for uncertainty spanning
multiple intervals, for large or asymmetric multiplicative uncertainty, or
for discrete association and selection uncertainty. Those cases require
nonlinear samples, a joint posterior, or a bounded sensitivity study.

\subsection{Response condition for the unit label}
\label{sec:response-equations}

Let \(P_B(\boldsymbol\omega)\) be the originating Beammap response template,
with declared coordinates and unit peak,
\begin{equation}
 P_B(\boldsymbol 0)=1.
 \label{eq:beam-peak}
\end{equation}
For an unresolved source of top-of-atmosphere flux density \(S\) mJy, a
downstream realized linear response \(L\) has ideal map peak
\begin{equation}
 m_{\rm peak}=S\rho_L\ \mjybeam,
 \qquad \rho_L=[L P_B](\boldsymbol 0).
 \label{eq:peak-response}
\end{equation}
The original point-source-peak label remains scientifically literal only when
\(\rho_L=1\) on the declared support. If a kernel or filter changes
\(\rho_L\), the consumer must either propagate an explicit response
renormalization and update the response-basis provenance, or withhold the
literal peak-calibration claim. SCI-CAL does not estimate \(\rho_L\).

For an explicitly selected elliptical Gaussian approximation, the originating
solid angle would be
\begin{equation}
 \Omega_B=\frac{\pi\theta_{\rm maj}\theta_{\rm min}}{4\ln 2},
 \label{eq:elliptical-solid-angle}
\end{equation}
with angle units, frame, position angle, and approximation label retained.
Equation~\eqref{eq:elliptical-solid-angle} records response basis only. It does
not authorize a surface-brightness conversion or integrated photometry in
v0.1.

\subsection{Canonical lineage reconstructibility}

Let \(\mathcal L_o\) denote one canonical calibration-lineage record per
coherent reduction package. For every valid occurrence, it must be possible to
resolve
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal L_o\longrightarrow
 \{x^{xs}_j,b_j,K^{\rm acq},R^{\rm APT},E^{\rm assoc},F^{\rm sel},
 \mathcal O_a,\tau_{225},X,C_a,Q,\mathcal V,\theta,P_B,L\}
 \longrightarrow M_j\longrightarrow y_j.
 \label{eq:reconstruction}
\end{equation}
The arrows mean resolvable scientific lineage, not a required file layout.
Compact product links may point to the canonical record and immutable APT;
they need not duplicate dense tables in every product.
